The major difference is that positivism says social life should be studied with natural-science methods (objective measurement, hypothesis testing, general causal laws), while naturalism says it should be studied in its natural settings and understood through participants' own meanings, without forcing it into that model. The team note's geographic claims don't hold up, so I haven't used them. Positivism came from Comte and others in the philosophy and sociology of science, not only from European jurists, and naturalism's roots (for example the Chicago School) don't fit a simple "outside Europe" label.

CONFIDENCE: 78
